archetype.name: Pocket Passer (rhythm and anticipation)
archetype.definition: A 5-foot-10 distributor who wins from the pocket by holding the ball, reading the middle of the field and now pushing it downfield more, with his legs a barely used afterthought (6 carries in four games).

report.headline: Year-four leap looks real in the pocket; the deep-ball efficiency won't hold.
report.take:
Four games into his fourth season, Bryce Young is playing like a different quarterback from the one in his career file. He sits at 0.24 EPA per dropback (11th of 42) after three seasons of -0.173, 0.006 and 0.01, and a 7.83 yards per attempt against a previous best of 6.3. Carolina has noticed. The Panthers pass 5.9 points more than the situation predicts, 4th in the league, which is a staff choosing to put the game on him behind a 21st-ranked run game.

The parts of the jump that look structural come from his pocket management and his ball placement. His pressure-to-sack rate has fallen every year, from 41.3% as a rookie to 24.2%, then 20.9%, and now 15.6% (6th of 32). His bad-throw rate is 11.7% after sitting between 15% and 21% for three years. He is holding the ball slightly longer (2.93s against 2.83 last year) and throwing farther (9.67 intended air yards against a 6.9 aDOT in 2025). That means he is reading the play out rather than bailing early. The middle of the field is where it shows most: 31 attempts at 0.633 EPA with a 17.4 CPOE.

The numbers also hide some things. A large share of the efficiency rides on 22 deep attempts at 0.972 EPA and a 15.8 CPOE. Twenty-two throws is a hint, not a baseline, and that level will come down. Third down has been poor: -0.034 EPA, a 35.9% conversion rate facing an average of 7.6 yards to go, and 6 of his 10 sacks. Seven red-zone touchdowns sit on a 48.3% completion rate and a 33% success rate, which reads as touchdown luck on low efficiency. Week 1's 361 yards came partly while chasing a 59-point opponent. The Cleveland game (25.6% bad throws, -5.9 EPA on 48 attempts in 12 mph wind) is a reminder the old floor still exists.

Carolina's offense is still productive with injuries piling up. Week 4 was his best game at 20.5 EPA, with Jalen Coker inactive and against the league's worst defense. The bye and a run of expected returns should help. Expect a quarterback who settles somewhere between average and good rather than staying top-10, which would still be the best version of him on record.

strengths.title: Pressure no longer turns into sacks
strengths.body: Only 15.6% of his pressures have become sacks, 6th best. That continues a four-year slide from 41.3% as a rookie. Because the improvement has built steadily over seasons, it reads as learned pocket feel rather than a hot streak. It matters more with Carolina's line banged up and allowing hits at a 23rd-ranked rate.

strengths.title: Cleaner ball placement over the middle
strengths.body: His bad-throw rate is down to 11.7% from 15.3% last year and 20.8% in 2024. The middle of the field has become his best area, with a 74.2% completion rate and a 17.4 CPOE on 31 throws. The accuracy gain is plausibly real given the longer-term trend, though the middle-of-field CPOE will cool on more volume.

strengths.title: Coaches are trusting him to carry it
strengths.body: A +5.9 pass rate over expected (4th) says the staff is leaning on him in neutral situations, and he is paying it back at 0.212 team pass EPA (8th). That volume holds as long as the run game sits at -0.159 EPA per carry. His 1,268 yards, most in the league, are built on it.

concerns.title: Deep-ball efficiency is running hot
concerns.body: Twenty-two deep attempts at 0.972 EPA with a 15.8 CPOE are carrying a lot of the per-play numbers. On a sample this small and this far above his history, that level will fall back. When it does, his overall EPA drifts from top-12 toward the middle of the pack.

concerns.title: Third down stalls, with sacks
concerns.body: On 39 third-down plays he has -0.034 EPA and 6 sacks, so most of his sacks come in obvious passing downs at 7.6 yards to go. That cost comes partly from holding the ball and partly from a line missing Ekwonu and Lewis. It is the clearest drag on drive success.

concerns.title: Red-zone TDs outrunning efficiency
concerns.body: He has 7 red-zone touchdowns on a 48.3% completion rate and 33% success. His 5.6% TD rate (14th) also sits well above his career norm. Expect fewer touchdowns per red-zone trip going forward.

trend.note: By EPA the four games went 15.5, 11.1, -5.9 and 20.5. Three were strong; Cleveland was a throwback dud with a 25.6% bad-throw rate and 4.2% aggressiveness. Week 4's best game came with a quicker 2.67s release and no Coker, though against the league's worst defense.

nextGame.headline: Clean pocket likely in Philadelphia, but deep shots get harder
nextGame.body:
Philadelphia's defense ranks 24th in EPA and 22nd against the pass. It is also the league's least disruptive front: 32nd in hit rate and 30th in sack rate. For a quarterback who wants time to read and throw over the middle, that is an inviting setup. The catch is that the Eagles defend deep balls well (6th in deep EPA), which is exactly where his 2026 efficiency has been inflated. Expect the yardage to have to come at short and intermediate depth. Philadelphia's offense is also weak (29th in EPA, passing 5.7 points below expected), so Carolina may not need the 41-to-48-attempt volume of its tighter games.

On Carolina's side, the bye lines up with expected returns. Coker and guard Damien Lewis both carry Oct. 18 estimated return dates, tackle Monroe Freeling could be back, and Trevor Etienne is due off IR. Coker matters most here: his 0.576 EPA per target is the best among Young's regular targets, and his return gives Young a real No. 2 beside McMillan. Ekwonu and Legette remain out. On Philadelphia's side, linebacker Zack Baun (concussion), safety Marcus Epps and corner Quinyon Mitchell (knee, questionable) were all injured as of Oct. 5. Those three would weaken the coverage at exactly the second and third levels Young attacks. Their listed return dates precede the game, so treat them as uncertain rather than out. The Eagles' offense is also missing DeVonta Smith, Dallas Goedert and Lane Johnson, with Barkley week-to-week, which tilts the expected script toward Carolina leading.

keyMatchups.title: No pass rush versus a patched line
keyMatchups.body: Philadelphia hits the quarterback less than anyone and ranks 30th in sack rate. That should cover for a Carolina line allowing a 23rd-ranked hit rate without Ekwonu. With his low pressure-to-sack rate, this is the setup most likely to cut his sack count.

keyMatchups.title: His deep game versus a stingy back end
keyMatchups.body: Young's deep throws have produced 0.972 EPA, while Philadelphia allows -0.132 on deep passes (6th). If Epps and Mitchell are back, expect the shots to be limited. The offense would then have to win at 10-19 yards, where he has posted 0.561 EPA.

keyMatchups.title: Game script against a weak offense
keyMatchups.body: Philadelphia ranks 29th in offensive EPA and plays run-leaning, now without several skill players and its right tackle. Carolina leading would mean fewer late dropbacks than his 40-attempt average. That trims the yardage ceiling without hurting efficiency.

nextGame.watch: Whether Young hits the intermediate middle once Philadelphia takes away the deep ball, especially if Baun is still out.

restOfSeason.body:
The parts of this season backed by multi-year trends should hold: the falling pressure-to-sack rate, the cleaner bad-throw rate and the coaches' willingness to throw. The parts resting on small samples should regress: a 15.8 CPOE on deep balls, a 6.1 overall CPOE against a career best near 1, and seven red-zone touchdowns on 33% red-zone success. Expect his EPA per dropback to settle closer to 0.05-0.15. That is still well above his first three seasons and roughly a middle-of-the-league starter.

Volume is the steadier piece. With a 21st-ranked run game and a high pass rate over expected, he should keep landing in the 35-40 attempt range. Yardage should be closer to 250-280 a game than the 317 he has averaged, since the Week 1 shootout and a Week 4 game against the 32nd-ranked defense inflated the early total. The offensive line is the swing piece. Lewis and Freeling returning would ease the third-down sack problem, and Ekwonu's absence into November keeps it from being fully solved.
swingFactors: Offensive line health (Lewis, Freeling, Ekwonu timeline)
Whether the deep-ball hit rate holds on more volume
Coker's return as a second efficient target

bets.reason: Philadelphia ranks 32nd in hit rate and 30th in sack rate. Young turns only 15.6% of pressures into sacks, and Lewis and Freeling may be back from the bye.

Philadelphia allows 241.3 passing yards per game to quarterbacks and ranks 6th against deep passes, the throws that padded his yardage. A 29th-ranked Eagles offense missing several skill players also points to a script with fewer late dropbacks.

confidence.note: Four games, a sharp break from his career baseline and a shifting offensive line; next-game line not yet posted.
